key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and contracting the lattice.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical design lever for proton-conducting SOFC electrolytes that can boost proton uptake/diffusion while reducing degradation from CO2/SO2 and impurity-phase formation.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site electronegativity and ionic radius effects
Assessment of proton transport, vacancy formation, and gas adsorption trends
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational results showing correlated changes in oxygen-vacancy formation, proton uptake/basicity, impurity-phase suppression, and reduced CO2/SO2 adsorption with Ca doping.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on whether proton transfer is rate-limiting and on controlling Ca surface segregation and grain-boundary effects in real electrolytes.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
